text:
sara: quick sync — we need to pick a default approach for GPUs across new k8s clusters. options on table: enable MIG profiles on A100/H100 nodes or move to time-sliced/vGPU-like runtime for higher packing. thoughts on autoscaler implications?

jordan: my 2c: MIG gives deterministic isolation but fragments shapes. autoscaler can't coalesce tiny leftover MIG slices across nodes, so bin-packing efficiency drops unless we align pod requests with MIG profiles.

sara: right. we've seen 20-30% wasted on staging when people request 1 GPU but MIG profiles are 1/7, 1/4, etc. nodepool explosion if we try to match every shape.

lee: can we avoid explosion by keeping a small set of canonical MIG shapes (e.g., 1g.5gb, 2g, full) and force pod-level resource requests to one of those? use admission webhook to rewrite/validate? :thinking_face:

jordan: yeah, admission webhook + mutating to round up is viable. downside: some training jobs that want exact vram will be overprovisioned. but overall cost wins.

ana: (ops metric) note: with MIG we saw cluster-autoscaler scale-up slower because provisioning specialized nodepools (migs-2g) required provider API calls for GPU partitioning, which takes longer and sometimes fails with rate limits. time-slice path on G5 had quicker scale-up but required licensing and we had noisy neighbors.

sara: good call. region constraints too: some regions only have A100 shapes, others G5. H100 doesn't support MIG in same way yet in our k8s plugin.

jordan: Implementation idea: keep 3 nodepools per region: "gpu-full" (no MIG, full GPU), "gpu-mig" (MIG-enabled with canonical shapes), and "gpu-preemptible" for cheap runs. Use taints/tolerations + nodeSelector for scheduling. autoscaler rules: prefer scale-up on "gpu-mig" for small jobs, fallback to "gpu-full" if packing fails.

lee: config example I sketched: 
```yaml
nodePool: gpu-mig
labels:
  gpu.instance-type: a100-mig
taints:
  - key: gpu-role
    value: mig
    effect: NoSchedule
resourceClasses: ["nvidia.com/mig-1g.5gb", "nvidia.com/mig-2g"]
```
This keeps CA aware of capacity classes.

ana: one more gotcha: cluster-autoscaler uses node-level resources. when device-plugin exposes 7 MIG devices on node, CA sees 7 discrete GPUs — but if pods ask for 1 GPU environment variable vs specific MIG profile, scheduler picks wrong ones. need to expose extended resources with explicit names and update our helm charts for device-plugin config.

jordan: agree. also add podPriority for long training jobs so CA won't scale-down nodes mid-run. we had a few jobs preempted during scale-down last week.

sara: cost side: time-slicing (vGPU) looked cheaper per-hour for small inference fleets, but we risk SLAs due to noisy neighbors and pinning is harder. Any data from canary cluster?

lee: canary: inference latency p95 increased ~15% under burst with time-slice enabled. MIG p95 stayed flat. so for latency-sensitive inference, MIG wins. for offline batch, time-slice can save $$ and reduce node count.

ana: ops action items:
- create webhook to normalize GPU requests to canonical MIG sizes
- update device-plugin config to expose extended resource names
- add CA predicate to prefer gpu-mig nodepool for small requests
- run a 2-week canary in us-west1 with both modes enabled and traffic split

k8s-bot: deploy job submitted: `deploy/canary/gpu-slicing-mode` (PR #4821) — status: pending CI :hourglass_flowing_sand:

jordan: let's also add a dashboard panel showing MIG slice fragmentation (fraction of unused MIG devices per node) + CA scale actions. helps quantify the wins before making org-wide default.

sara: agreed. prioritize webhook and device-plugin change. I'll schedule a 30-min sync tomorrow to lock defaults after canary data. thanks all :thumbsup:
